doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Cage on songs, cane work, records and family
title: Cage recalls a slavery-time song his mother sang
summary: Cage recites a song his mother used to sing, a racist slavery-time verse; the interviewer says it must date from slavery.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Okay, we got the second reel of James Butch Cage on May the 13th, 1967. What do you want to say now? What do you want to say?

My mama used to have one song called Black Nigga Baby, Black Feet and Shiny Eyes, Black all over in the bone the other way with any rubber feet. And they turn that nigga around and knock him in the head and the white folks say you got to kill the nigga dead.
What was that, was the song?

That was the song? That's the song. Some white folks, they'd hug him in the flinty, some don't get so fat, my Danny. I want to take a dagger, eat the meat and chew the grizzles, get up in the morning and be free.
